Among some of Netflix's finest releases, there are a select few that truly stand out, solid gems that are often discussed alongside some of TV's all-time greatest. The shows are ranked based on the strength of their writing, performances, visual identity, cultural impact, consistency, and overall contribution to Netflix's reputation for prestige television.

8
'Blue Eye Samurai' (2023–Present)
https://static0.colliderimages.com/wordpress/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/blue-eye-samurai-maya-erskine-ming-na-wen.jpg?q=70&fit=crop&w=825&dpr=1

blocks.x: Image via Netflix

Blue Eye Samurai is one of Netflix’s more recent animated masterpieces that already stands as one of the platform’s greats. Blue Eye Samurai is set in 17th-century Edo-period Japan, following the sword master, Mizu (Maya Erskine), who is traveling disguised as a man as she pursues foreign men who may be connected to her birth.

Blue Eye Samurai earns its place in this discussion of TV’s all-time greatest because it transforms revenge into something beautiful, emotionally captivating, and extraordinarily brutal. The series masterfully connects action to shame, identity, rejection, and survival. Blue Eye Samurai may essentially be the “new kid” on the block, but it's definitely left its mark on those who have happened across the incredibly entertaining action series. Its composition borrows from Japanese art, chanbara, westerns, graphic novels, and live-action blocking, all without ever settling into imitation, marking it as one of the most powerful viewing experiences that masterfully carries the weight of classic samurai storytelling.
https://static0.colliderimages.com/wordpress/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/sense8-jamie-clayton-freeman-agyeman.jpg?q=70&fit=crop&w=825&dpr=1
blocks.c: Jamie Clayton and Freeman Agyeman in Sense8

blocks.x: Image via Netflix

Sense8 easily makes this list, even when it's one of Netflix’s most underrated sci-fi gems. The series follows eight strangers across the globe — police officer Will Gorski (Brian J. Smith), DJ Riley Blue (Tuppence Middleton), hacker Nomi Marks (Jamie Clayton), actor Lito Rodriguez (Miguel Ángel Silvestre), pharmacist Kala Dandekar (Tina Desai), businesswoman and fighter Sun Bak (Bae Doona), safe-cracker Wolfgang Bogdanow (Max Riemelt), and bus driver Capheus Onyango (Toby Onwumere) — as they realize they share a connection that allows them to experience one another’s memories, skills, emotions, thoughts, languages, and danger.

From epic visuals to a masterful action story, Sense8 stands as a quality series that is far too rarely talked about. The show lingers among the greatest of TV because it's genuinely one of Netflix’s most ambitious works of art. Very few television shows even come close to matching its boldness and sincerity. With its premise exploring love, culture, sexuality, and identity across different lives and countries, Sense8 earns its status as a rare great that is worthy of all-time recognition.
https://static0.colliderimages.com/wordpress/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/ozark-jason-bateman-1.jpg?q=70&fit=crop&w=825&dpr=1
blocks.c: Jason Bateman looking to the side, about to get into a car in Ozark.

blocks.x: Image via Netflix

This crime drama leaves its mark on its viewers because it consistently builds tension. Ozark centers around Marty Byrde (Jason Bateman), a financial adviser, who moves his family to the Missouri Ozarks after a money-laundering scheme for the Mexican drug cartel goes wrong and forces him to launder millions more, while desperately trying to keep himself and his family safe.

Ozark is one of the best crime series produced by Netflix, and it has earned its spot in discussions regarding the platform’s all-time greatest because it transforms what could have been a pretty generic crime premise into a relentless story about survival, family, and moral collapse. The show is a bundle of tension as it makes every choice feel dangerous, even when characters are in mostly quiet moments, biding their time. Ozark is quite the thrilling watch that Netflix subscribers have frequently praised for its efforts in showcasing an intense and incredibly unpredictable crime story, easily making it a genuinely fantastic all-time great among TV’s best, for that alone.

blocks.x: Image via Netflix

4
'Black Mirror' (2011–Present)
https://static0.colliderimages.com/wordpress/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/img_8439-1.jpg?q=49&fit=crop&w=825&dpr=2
blocks.c: A man in a space suit in Black Mirror

blocks.x: Image via Netflix

Black Mirror is Netflix's brilliant anthology sci-fi series that’s quite easy to debate, discuss, and genuinely remember. Each of the series' episodes is a complete story, which often uses technology, artificial intelligence, media, surveillance, and digital obsession to expose something quite chilling about human behavior.

Black Mirror is practically a Netflix icon, one that often delivers episodes that feel like short films which stay in the mind long after the credits roll. The anthology series may not have invented technological dystopia, but it definitely updated The Twilight Zone's model for social platforms, smartphones, virtual identity, machine learning, and platform capitalism with enough clarity that the series has become one of TV’s most unsettling and brilliantly recognizable examinations of humanity’s increasing dependence on modern tech. Black Mirror is absolutely one of Netflix’s bleakest series, but it also happens to be one of the platform's defining greats.
https://static0.colliderimages.com/assets/images/sr-db-logo-icon-colored-dark.svg?v=1.9
https://static0.colliderimages.com/wordpress/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/jinx-sacrifice-arcane-finale-1.jpg?q=70&fit=crop&w=825&dpr=1
Image via Netflix

This Netflix animated series easily earns its place among TV’s all-time greatest. Adapted from the League of Legends universe, Arcane is set in the divided world of Piltover and Zaun, centering on sisters Vi (Hailee Steinfeld) and Powder, later known as Jinx (Ella Purnell), whose relationship is ripped apart due to tragedy as political tensions rise and conflict between the two cities threatens to change their lives forever.

Arcane is not only visually stunning, but it is also emotionally devastating. The Netflix animation is both confident and extremely controlled. There is no doubt that it's one of the streaming platform’s greatest masterpieces, which defiantly raised the bar for what animated TV and adaptations in general could achieve. Arcane is incredibly beautiful, so much so that viewers are able to pause at almost any frame and be hit with a face full of wonder. But in reality, its beauty isn’t even the show’s greatest strength; no, in fact, its most incredible achievements come from the tragedy of its characters and the consequences of their choices. Arcane is a memorable watch that lands itself on this list because, with visuals alone, it outpaces several in its genre.

2
'BoJack Horseman' (2014–2020)
https://static0.colliderimages.com/wordpress/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/bojack-horseman-view-from-halfway-down-beatrice.jpeg?q=70&fit=crop&w=825&dpr=1
blocks.c: Beatrice and BoJack facing each other in 'BoJack Horseman's Season 6 episode "The View From Halfway Down"

blocks.x: Image via Netflix

BoJack Horseman masterfully mixes absurdity, sadness, emotional realism, and satire, becoming one of Netflix’s most defining animated shows. Set in a world populated by humans and anthropomorphic animals, the series focuses on BoJack Horseman (Will Arnett), a washed-up 1990s sitcom star, who is trying to reignite his fame while tackling addiction, loneliness, depression, and crippling depression.

BoJack Horseman does initially look like a pretty absurd Hollywood cartoon, but it's quite the emotional series. The show is actually extremely bleak, a mirror held up to its audience, as it doles out painfully honest examinations of depression, trauma, and the difficulty of trying to become a truly better person after repeatedly hurting those that matter. BoJack Horseman can easily claim its status as an all-time great because it’s incredibly raw and real, with a story that refuses to make light of rather serious topics and a protagonist who's extremely flawed, making it an icon in its own right.

1
'Mindhunter' (2017–2019)
https://static0.colliderimages.com/wordpress/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/jonathan-groff-in-mindhunter.jpg?q=70&fit=crop&w=825&dpr=1
blocks.c: Jonathan Groff in a suit and tie walking through a prison in Mindhunter.

blocks.x: Image via Netflix

This underrated masterpiece is definitely worthy of the status as one of the all-time greatest shows ever made because it transforms crime investigation into something deeply unsettling, quiet, and intelligent. Mindhunter focuses on FBI agents Bill Tench (Holt McCallany) and Holden Ford (Jonathan Groff), who begin interviewing imprisoned serial killers in the hopes of understanding how they think and using their findings to help solve ongoing murder cases.

Mindhunter doesn’t rely on constant scenes of fast-paced arrests or acts of violence, but instead spends its runtime focusing on the difficult conversations that eventually sparked change in how serial killers were being understood. The series stands out because very few Netflix dramas are as impeccably controlled or psychologically sharp, as it delivers a fantastic procedural idea but expertly elevates it with a chilling study of obsession, behavior, power, and the language people tend to use when explaining terrible deeds. Mindhunter is one of the most deserving to be recognized as an all-time great Netflix watch because there’s never a dull moment with the captivating series, with episode after episode of brilliant precision.

The anthology series may not have invented technological dystopia, but it definitely updated The Twilight Zone's model for social platforms, smartphones, virtual identity, machine learning, and platform capitalism with enough clarity that the series has become one of TV’s most unsettling and brilliantly recognizable examinations of humanity’s increasing dependence on modern tech. Black Mirror is absolutely one of Netflix’s bleakest series, but it also happens to be one of the platform's defining greats.

3
'Arcane' (2021–2024)

Image via Netflix

This Netflix animated series easily earns its place among TV’s all-time greatest. Adapted from the League of Legends universe, Arcane is set in the divided world of Piltover and Zaun, centering on sisters Vi (Hailee Steinfeld) and Powder, later known as Jinx (Ella Purnell), whose relationship is ripped apart due to tragedy as political tensions rise and conflict between the two cities threatens to change their lives forever.

Arcane is not only visually stunning, but it is also emotionally devastating. The Netflix animation is both confident and extremely controlled. There is no doubt that it's one of the streaming platform’s greatest masterpieces, which defiantly raised the bar for what animated TV and adaptations in general could achieve. Arcane is incredibly beautiful, so much so that viewers are able to pause at almost any frame and be hit with a face full of wonder. But in reality, its beauty isn’t even the show’s greatest strength; no, in fact, its most incredible achievements come from the tragedy of its characters and the consequences of their choices. Arcane is a memorable watch that lands itself on this list because, with visuals alone, it outpaces several in its genre.

2
'BoJack Horseman' (2014–2020)

Image via Netflix

BoJack Horseman masterfully mixes absurdity, sadness, emotional realism, and satire, becoming one of Netflix’s most defining animated shows. Set in a world populated by humans and anthropomorphic animals, the series focuses on BoJack Horseman (Will Arnett), a washed-up 1990s sitcom star, who is trying to reignite his fame while tackling addiction, loneliness, depression, and crippling depression.

BoJack Horseman does initially look like a pretty absurd Hollywood cartoon, but it's quite the emotional series. The show is actually extremely bleak, a mirror held up to its audience, as it doles out painfully honest examinations of depression, trauma, and the difficulty of trying to become a truly better person after repeatedly hurting those that matter. BoJack Horseman can easily claim its status as an all-time great because it’s incredibly raw and real, with a story that refuses to make light of rather serious topics and a protagonist who's extremely flawed, making it an icon in its own right.

1
'Mindhunter' (2017–2019)

Image via Netflix

This underrated masterpiece is definitely worthy of the status as one of the all-time greatest shows ever made because it transforms crime investigation into something deeply unsettling, quiet, and intelligent. Mindhunter focuses on FBI agents Bill Tench (Holt McCallany) and Holden Ford (Jonathan Groff), who begin interviewing imprisoned serial killers in the hopes of understanding how they think and using their findings to help solve ongoing murder cases.

Mindhunter doesn’t rely on constant scenes of fast-paced arrests or acts of violence, but instead spends its runtime focusing on the difficult conversations that eventually sparked change in how serial killers were being understood. The series stands out because very few Netflix dramas are as impeccably controlled or psychologically sharp, as it delivers a fantastic procedural idea but expertly elevates it with a chilling study of obsession, behavior, power, and the language people tend to use when explaining terrible deeds. Mindhunter is one of the most deserving to be recognized as an all-time great Netflix watch because there’s never a dull moment with the captivating series, with episode after episode of brilliant precision.
